title: Test behavior, not implementation details
subtitle: Write tests that survive refactoring
learning_objective: Choose assertions that verify observable behavior rather than internal call sequences.

source_refs.title: Martin Fowler: Unit Test
source_refs.supports: unit testing concepts and test boundaries

scenes.title: THE FRAGILE TEST
scenes.body: A harmless refactor changes a private helper and breaks 30 tests—even though the feature still works.

scenes.title: Assert the contract
scenes.body: A useful test checks observable inputs and outputs or externally meaningful effects. Tests tightly coupled to internal method calls make refactoring expensive.

scenes.title: Prefer an outcome
When interactions matter
scenes.body: Mock or assert a dependency interaction when it is part of the contract—such as ensuring a payment is not charged twice.

scenes.question: Which test is usually more resilient?
options: One asserting a private helper was called 4 times
One asserting the public result is correct
scenes.explanation: The public result is the behavior users depend on; private implementation details can change during refactoring.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Test behavior that matters to callers. Assert implementation details only when they are genuinely part of the contract.
